questionText: Consider $4 \times 4$ matrices with their elements from $\{0, 1\}$. The number of such matrices with even number of $1$s in every row and every column is
explanation:
Step 1: Understand the submatrix freedoms
For an $n \times n$ binary matrix where every row and column contains an even number of $1$s, the entries in the upper-left $(n-1) \times (n-1)$ submatrix can be chosen freely.

Step 2: Determine remaining elements uniquely
• For each of the first $n-1$ rows, the element in the $n$-th column is uniquely fixed to make the row sum even.
• For each of the first $n-1$ columns, the element in the $n$-th row is uniquely fixed to make the column sum even.
• The bottom-right element $a_{n,n}$ is uniquely and consistently determined by both the $n$-th row and $n$-th column parity constraints.

Step 3: Calculate total valid matrices
For a $4 \times 4$ matrix ($n = 4$), the free submatrix contains $(4 - 1) \times (4 - 1) = 3 \times 3 = 9$ entries.
Since each entry has $2$ possible choices ($0$ or $1$):
$$\text{Total matrices} = 2^9 = 512$$

Therefore, the number of such matrices is 512 (Option A).
